messages.text: During the page yesterday, @ask-oncall found the CoreDNS runbook and the Kubernetes debugging DNS page in like 3 seconds. That was actually useful, not just a link dump.

replies.text: nice, did it land on the right bit or just search the whole wiki?
Right bit. It pointed me at the DNS resolution checklist and the `kubectl -n kube-system logs deploy/coredns` bit immediately.

messages.text: Can it read the Postgres docs too, or is it only wiki pages we already had indexed? Asking because that would be pretty handy for pg-feeds stuff.

replies.text: that would save a bunch of tab hunting for me too

messages.text: Yes, a subset is vendored. It can answer from the Postgres runbooks, the PgBouncer notes, and the Patroni migration docs that we copied into the internal knowledge bundle.

replies.text: oh nice, so not live crawling the whole wiki?
Right, curated set only. Less surprise, fewer stale edges.

messages.text: Good. The DNS answer was a lot better than me grepping random docs while watching the alert flap.

replies.text: what did it suggest, if you remember?
It told me to check kube-dns upstream reachability first, then the CoreDNS configmap, then whether the node had broken resolv.conf. Which was basically the path we ended up taking.

messages.text: If it can surface the pgbouncer-feeds admin port docs too, that would be perfect. I always forget the exact `psql` incantation for transaction pooling checks.

replies.text: It has the admin console notes, yes. No direct actions though, just read-only guidance.

messages.text: That feels like the right line. Helpful, but not trying to be an autopilot for prod changes.

replies.text: agreed. if it starts trying to `kubectl apply` stuff, i'm out
It won't. Read-only only, and it prefers linking the exact doc section over improvising.

messages.text: Can we get more of the pg-feeds troubleshooting pages vendored next? The replica lag one would be useful for oncall.

replies.text: Yep, I can add that. If you have a doc that keeps getting used in pages, send it over and I will pull it into the bundle.

messages.text: Honestly this is the first time I've used it mid-page and not regretted it. Keep going.

replies.text: same, shipped enough value to keep around
Thanks, that is the kind of feedback we need. If you spot a bad answer, drop it in this channel with the query and the doc it missed.
